newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to put on trial 37 charged with militancy.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to put on trial 37 charged with militancy.

text.p: Egypt will put on trial 36 men and a teenage boy charged with belonging to the country's biggest Moslem militant group and planning to murder state officials, security sources said on Thursday.
They said police arrested the men in Cairo in 1996 while they were trying to rob a gold shop belonging to an Egyptian Christian.
Their charges also include planning to rob 18 other gold shops, plotting to kill police officers and possessing weapons and explosives, the sources said.

No date has been set but the charge sheet obtained on Thursday said the 37 belong to the militant Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), which regards Christians, tourists, policemen and state officials as legitimate targets in its armed struggle to overthrow the state.
More than 1,000 people have been killed and scores more wounded since the group began its activities in 1992.

The sources said they do not know whether the teenager, Amr Hassanein, would be tried as a child or under a new law allowing the trial and imprisonment of suspected militants who are less than 18 years old.
Previously, under-aged militants would be tried in juvenile courts and sent to a home for young offenders.
This week, a suspected Moslem militant teenager went on trial in a state security court on charges of killing five policemen and two civilians when he was 14 years old.
